source.quote: Musetec's own manual for the MH-DA006MINI, read 2026-11-25; « Speciﬁcations » on page 10: « DAC Chips   Es9039pro » - no multiplier, unlike the DA006's « Es9039pro*2 ». « USB Port   P CM 44.1K~384K 24/32bit » and « DSD 64~ DSD 512 ». « S/P DIF Input   CO AX 1 / CO AX2 / AE S / OPT » with « P CM44.1K~192K 16~24bit » and « DOP 64x ». « I2S input   P CM 44.1K~768K 24/32bit », « DSD 64~ DSD1024 », « DOP 64~256 ». « Analog Output   RCA: 2.5Vrms / X LR: 5Vrms » and « THD+N > 117dB (A-weighting) ». Rear panel, page 4: « (1) USB input  (2) Bluetooth antenna  (3) COAX1 S/PDIF input  (4) I2S input  (5) Optical S/PDIF input  (6) A ES/EBU input  (7) CO AX2 S/P DIF input », and the input-channel table adds « BT  Bluetooh input » - the typo is the maker's. Same six named filter modes as the DA006. From DA006MINI_detail.html: « 4. Amanero USB module, support formats up to PCM384K or DSD512. » and « 8. THD+N 127dB. » - and that page opens « The main features of SA001 are as follows. », the maker's own copy-paste error, SA001 being its pre-amplifier.

facts.chip: « DAC Chips   Es9039pro », ONE, where the DA006's table says « Es9039pro*2 ». The USB stage is named on the maker's page: « Amanero USB module ».

device_settings.why: SIX positions, all six NAMED, from the remote's FILT key: « Lin Phase Fast / Linear Phase Fast Roll-oﬀ », « Lin Phase Slow », « Min Phase Fast », « Min Phase Slow », « Min Phase » and « Lin Phase APO / Linear Phase Apodizing ». The manual says « There are 6 ﬁlter modes » and the settings menu confirms « Total of 6 digital ﬁlter modes can be selected. » No OFF or bypass position exists among the six.

_conditions_NON_CONCLUANTES_chez_Musetec: No terms page found on mu-sound.com, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding none. Measured 2026-11-25: the whole navigation was checked, HOME / ABOUT US / PRODUCTS / SUPPORT / CONTACT and their _cn twins, and no legal, terms, copyright or privacy link exists; terms.html, legal.html, copyright.html, terms-of-use.html, privacy.html, tos.html and disclaimer.html all 404. robots.txt returns 404, so no Content-Signal and no Claude group exist because the file does not. Footer on every page: « Copyright (c) 2023   MUSETEC Audio   All rights reserved ». The site is plain HTTP; HTTPS is not served.
_lksaudio_com_NEST_PAS_ce_fabricant: A host trap worth recording. Musetec traded as L.K.S Audio until 2019 - its own About page says « Initially used to be called L.K.S Audio, with MH-DA002/DA003/DA004/DA005 [...] Since 2019, the new brand MUSETEC has been launched » - but lksaudio.com is a DIFFERENT company: « LAIKESI », a Chinese factory for mixers, professional amplifiers, microphones and speakers. It was not used. And its robots.txt does carry an explicit group naming ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User and anthropic-ai whose directives end « Allow: / » - a permission that governs the wrong company and is irrelevant here. Second time today a plausible domain turned out to belong to someone else, after MUSICIAN's parked musicianaudio.com.
_les_ligatures_de_ces_PDF_sont_PRESENTES: Worth stating because today has produced three different extraction failures. These manuals were extracted in DEFAULT pdftotext mode and their ligatures come through as single Unicode characters - the documents print « Speciﬁcations », « Roll-oﬀ », « diﬀerent », « ﬁrmware » - and they are left exactly as extracted rather than normalised. What IS lost is word spacing, « PCM44.1K~192K », which is the PDFs' own kerning. So nothing is missing here, unlike Shanling's manuals where -layout ate every « t », Sabaj's D4 where the document itself has no mapping for ti and fi, and VMV's English tables which have no text layer at all.
_le_SPDIF_est_donne_en_UN_SEUL_rang_grou: Every Musetec specification table gives one combined row for its S/PDIF family - « COAX 1 / COAX2 / AE S / OPT » here, « COAX / BNC / AES / OPT » on the older models - so the maker states coaxial, AES/EBU and optical JOINTLY and never separately. The same figure is therefore written to each of those keys in `inputs`, which is the maker's own grouping and not an inference; no separate figure was invented for any one of them.
_aucun_mode_NOS_et_le_mot_bypass_veut_di: The string NOS appears nowhere in Musetec's pages or manuals, so the non-oversampling against New-Old-Stock ambiguity never arose, and no model states an oversampling bypass or a filter-OFF position. The only « bypass » wording on this maker's site is « power supply bypass filters », which are capacitors, and the volume « BYP » key on the DA004 and DA005 remotes. `correctable` is written on no Musetec record. « Native DSD » is never stated in words either, for any model - DoP is, as « DOP 64x » and « DOP 64~256 ».
_son_I2S_accepte_DEUX_FOIS_ce_que_son_US: « USB Port   P CM 44.1K~384K » and « DSD 64~ DSD 512 » against « I2S input   P CM 44.1K~768K » and « DSD 64~ DSD1024 ». The I2S socket takes twice the PCM rate and twice the DSD of the USB one, on a device whose USB stage is an « Amanero USB module ». That is the reverse of the usual shape, where USB is the fast socket and everything else trails it - and `pcm_max_hz` and `dsd_max` therefore describe the I2S input, not the USB one, which is exactly why the per-socket figures matter more than the device figure.
_le_THD_N_est_publie_DEUX_FOIS_avec_dix_: « THD+N > 117dB (A-weighting) » in the manual's specification table against « 8. THD+N 127dB. » on both DA006MINI_detail.html and products.html. Ten decibels, two documents, one product. Nothing is recorded - this catalogue holds no distortion figure - and it is quoted because it is a measure of how closely this maker's two publication channels agree, which bears on every other figure taken from either.
